items.text: Maria Pappas has been Cook County Treasurer since 1998. She previously served two terms as a Cook County Commissioner. She also works as an attorney and has a private therapy practice.

sentences.text: Maria Pappas has been Cook County Treasurer since 1998.
She previously served two terms as a Cook County Commissioner.
She also works as an attorney and has a private therapy practice.

items.text: She advocated for the Cook County Debt Disclosure Ordinance, passed in 2009. The ordinance requires taxing districts to publicly report their finances, including pension debt. In 2026, her office reported that local governments sought $743.8 million in new property taxes, with homeowners paying the bulk of the hike. A study from her office found that Cook County property taxes doubled the rate of inflation over the past 30 years. She supported property tax reforms that were signed into law in 2026. The reforms phase out county tax-lien sales to help homeowners catch up with property taxes before losing their homes. The Cook County Democratic Party states her 'Black and Latino Houses Matter' initiative returned more than $120 million to owners in minority communities through refunds and exemptions.

items.text: Her campaign says that when she took office, she found $30 million in uncashed checks and moved to modernize operations with technology. The Cook County Democratic Party states she reduced staff from 250 to 58 employees and increased interest earnings on deposits from $4.8 million to nearly $18 million in her first year.
